title: New Mexico's 2nd Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The general election for New Mexico's 2nd Congressional District pits two-term Democratic incumbent Rep. Gabe Vasquez against Republican nominee Greg Cunningham, a Marine Corps veteran and former Albuquerque police detective. The district, which covers southern and western New Mexico including Las Cruces, Carlsbad, and parts of Albuquerque, has been highly competitive in recent cycles — Vasquez won by narrow margins in both 2022 (flipping the seat) and 2024. With national ratings agencies calling the race Lean D to Toss Up, control of this swing seat could factor into which party holds the U.S. House majority. Key contrasts include border security, the economy, public safety, and energy policy.
polling_note: Only one publicly available horserace poll was found: a Republican-aligned NRCC survey from late April 2026 showing a statistically tied race (Vasquez 43%, Cunningham 41%). No independent or Democratic-sponsored polls were located.

candidates.name: Gabe Vasquez
candidates.summary: Incumbent U.S. Rep. Gabe Vasquez is seeking a third term representing New Mexico's 2nd Congressional District. A first-generation Mexican-American and Las Cruces native, he previously served on the Las Cruces City Council and as a field representative for U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich. In Congress, Vasquez has focused on lowering costs, public lands conservation, supporting veterans, and expanding rural broadband access.

candidates.name: Greg Cunningham
candidates.summary: Greg Cunningham is a Republican candidate for U.S. House in New Mexico's 2nd Congressional District. A Marine Corps combat veteran who served as a Recon Marine, he later spent 20 years as a detective with the Albuquerque Police Department, working on cartel and gang-related violent crime. Cunningham is a small business owner and previously ran unsuccessfully for the New Mexico House of Representatives in 2022 and 2024.
